title: Awesome Recursive Self-Critiquing
description: A curated, evaluation-first catalog of recursive self-critiquing and recursive self-improvement research, benchmarks, projects, and industry systems.

include: Explicit evaluation of critique, correction, recursive depth, or iterative improvement
Scalable oversight and weak-to-strong supervision protocols
Evaluators or reward models that participate in an improvement loop
Executable environments that measure improvement of AI artifacts or future agent behavior
Industry systems with public technical evidence for an evaluation-feedback-improvement workflow
exclude: Generic LLM-as-a-judge work without an improvement or oversight connection
Single-pass reflection without controlled baselines or held-out evaluation
General agent, RL, observability, or AutoML platforms without a measured improvement loop
Marketing claims without enough public methodology to identify what improved and how it was measured

resources.name: Scalable Oversight for Superhuman AI via Recursive Self-Critiquing
resources.relevance: Directly evaluates response, critique, and C2/C3 chains across Human-Human, Human-AI, and AI-AI oversight settings.
resources.scope_note: The central contribution is an oversight protocol and its evaluation, not unrestricted autonomous weight-level self-improvement.

resources.name: A Benchmark for Scalable Oversight Protocols
resources.relevance: Introduces a protocol-agnostic benchmark and Agent Score Difference for testing whether oversight advantages truth-telling over deception.
resources.scope_note: Debate is a demonstration within a broader oversight benchmark rather than evidence that debate alone solves scalable oversight.

resources.name: On Scalable Oversight with Weak LLMs Judging Strong LLMs
resources.relevance: Compares debate, consultancy, and direct question answering under controlled capability asymmetries.
resources.scope_note: Results are mixed outside information-asymmetric question answering and should not be generalized to all oversight tasks.

resources.name: LLM Critics Help Catch LLM Bugs
resources.relevance: Tests whether model-generated critiques improve human oversight of model-written code and measures hallucinated bug reports.
resources.scope_note: The evaluated improvement is human oversight quality, not autonomous recursive self-improvement.

resources.name: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
resources.relevance: Provides an empirical template for evaluating oversight on tasks where specialists outperform unaided humans and current models.
resources.scope_note: This is a measurement framework and precursor rather than a recursive critique system.

resources.name: RealCritic: Towards Effectiveness-Driven Evaluation of Language Model Critiques
resources.relevance: Evaluates critique quality through the corrections caused by self-critique, cross-critique, and iterative critique.
resources.scope_note: Correction effectiveness is the primary endpoint; it does not establish persistent model-level improvement.

resources.name: CAST: Critique-Aware Supervision for Training Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Calling Agents
resources.relevance: Evaluates action-level critic calibration, correction after feedback, resistance, repeated-run reliability, verification interactions, and cost.
resources.scope_note: CAST uses a separate actor and critic rather than higher-order self-critique, and its current policy training is supervised rather than on-policy.

resources.name: CriticBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Critique-Correct Reasoning
resources.relevance: Separates generation, critique, and correction across reasoning and coding datasets to localize failures in the loop.
resources.scope_note: The benchmark diagnoses component capability and does not by itself demonstrate a persistent self-improving system.

resources.name: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
resources.relevance: Defines evaluation pitfalls and boundary conditions for intrinsic and externally guided self-correction.
resources.scope_note: It is a survey and evaluation checklist rather than a new recursive self-correction method.

resources.name: Mind the Gap: Examining the Self-Improvement Capabilities of Large Language Models
resources.relevance: Formalizes the generation-verification gap and tests whether self-evaluation contains enough signal to improve a generator.
resources.scope_note: Improvement depends on the verification, filtering, reweighting, and distillation setup rather than reflection alone.

resources.name: Meta-Rewarding Language Models: Self-Improving Alignment with LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge
resources.relevance: Uses a meta-judge to evaluate the model's own judgments and counter saturation in self-rewarding loops.
resources.scope_note: The meta-judge remains part of the same synthetic feedback ecosystem and may share its biases.

resources.name: Self-Taught Evaluators
resources.relevance: Iteratively improves an evaluator from synthetic contrasts, reasoning traces, and regenerated judgments without labeled preference data.
resources.scope_note: Evaluation focuses on judge quality such as RewardBench rather than broader autonomous system improvement.

resources.name: Self-Generated Critiques Boost Reward Modeling for Language Models
resources.relevance: Tests whether generated and filtered natural-language critiques improve scalar reward prediction and downstream evaluation.
resources.scope_note: The critic-enhanced reward model is one component of an improvement pipeline rather than a complete RSI system.

resources.name: Critique-out-Loud Reward Models
resources.relevance: Generates an explicit critique before scalar reward prediction and evaluates preference accuracy and Best-of-N utility.
resources.scope_note: Explicit critique improves an evaluator but is not itself recursive unless embedded in a larger loop.

resources.name: Features as Rewards: Scalable Supervision for Open-Ended Tasks via Interpretability
resources.relevance: Uses frozen-model feature probes to evaluate hallucinations and candidate corrections, then feeds those signals into policy training and test-time selection.
resources.scope_note: The reported 58% reduction covers the full policy-plus-probing system; only part is attributable to learned policy change, and the pipeline is externally designed rather than recursively self-improving.

resources.name: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
resources.relevance: Compares matched rubric-free and rubric-guided revision across rounds, models, agent harnesses, and research benchmarks.
resources.scope_note: AutoSciRub improves research artifacts and the inference-time workflow rather than underlying model weights.

resources.name: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
resources.relevance: Tests whether agents can modify training algorithms in frozen repositories and generalize through fresh retraining and hidden evaluation.
resources.scope_note: The benchmark measures algorithm-design capability under bounded tasks, not open-ended recursive self-improvement.

resources.name: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
resources.relevance: Uses matched fresh-session sequences to test whether retained experience causally improves later tasks through the intended memory pathway.
resources.scope_note: The target is persistent agent behavior through memory rather than model-weight self-improvement.

resources.name: RSI-Exam: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement through Executable Research
resources.relevance: Uses development and sealed evaluation environments to measure whether agents improve methods or harnesses and generalize to hidden data.
resources.scope_note: It does not claim unrestricted or weight-level recursive self-improvement.

resources.name: RE-Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI R&D Capabilities of Language Model Agents Against Human Experts
resources.relevance: Provides open-ended ML research-engineering environments and human-expert baselines across time budgets.
resources.scope_note: RE-Bench measures a prerequisite AI R&D capability and is not an RSI test by itself.

resources.name: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
resources.relevance: Evaluates a language-model-infused improver that rewrites its own scaffolding against an explicit utility function.
resources.scope_note: The scaffold improves recursively while the underlying language model weights remain fixed.

resources.name: dots studio — dots3 / dots3-note Preview
resources.relevance: Documents a Proof-Verify-Refine system with repeated critique, review, correction, and synthesis.
resources.scope_note: The open preview model and internal IMO system should not be treated as identical; a full dots3 technical report remains pending.

resources.name: Goodfire — Silico / Interpretability-Guided Improvement
resources.relevance: Demonstrates interpretability-derived evaluators used as rewards for weight-level training and as iterative feedback for test-time correction and diffusion search.
resources.scope_note: Public evidence supports evaluator-guided model and search improvement, not autonomous or open-ended RSI; Silico's autonomous iteration lacks a public end-to-end RSI benchmark.

resources.name: Patronus AI
resources.relevance: Provides groundedness evaluation, explainable rubric scoring, trace-level failure diagnosis, and prompt-improvement proposals.
resources.scope_note: Evaluation infrastructure can support an improvement loop but is not evidence of recursive self-improvement by itself.

resources.name: Braintrust
resources.relevance: Connects production traces, datasets, experiments, reusable scorers, regression tracking, and proposed system changes.
resources.scope_note: The platform enables continual evaluation workflows but does not establish RSI without a measured closed-loop deployment.

resources.name: METR
resources.relevance: Measures autonomous AI R&D capability against human experts and across time budgets in open environments.
resources.scope_note: AI R&D capability is a prerequisite for some RSI pathways but is not equivalent to recursive self-improvement.

resources.name: The Anthropic Institute — When AI Builds Itself
resources.relevance: Frames progress toward automated AI R&D through public benchmarks, internal productivity evidence, telemetry, oversight, validation, and verification gaps.
resources.scope_note: This is an industry measurement perspective rather than an independently reproducible RSI benchmark.
